resources.name: Configuration
resources.doc:
One authored configuration at one layer, optionally inheriting from another. The parent
chain is what "composition" means here; resolution walks it and the nearest assignment wins.

fields.name: layerOrdinal
fields.doc:
Snapshot of `layer.ordinal`, validated on write, so the precedence rule below stays
within one reference hop.

resources.name: ConfigurationLayer
resources.doc:
Layers give resolution a deterministic order. The ordinal is the precedence: a higher
layer's assignment wins, and equal ordinals are impossible because the key is unique.

resources.name: ParameterAssignment
resources.doc:
An assignment of one parameter in one configuration. Exactly one of a literal value or a
secret reference, decided by the parameter's own type rather than by the caller.

resources.name: ParameterDefinition
resources.doc:
A parameter a pinned specification declares. Pinning is what makes "typed" mean anything:
the same key may be a boolean in one revision and an integer in the next, and a
configuration authored against the old revision must not silently retype.

fields.name: secret
fields.doc:
Snapshot of `valueType.secret`, validated on write. Kernel expressions hydrate one
reference hop, so every rule that needs to know "is this secret" would otherwise be
reaching through two. Snapshotting it here keeps those rules enforceable.

resources.name: ParameterType
resources.doc:
What choices parameterize a thing, typed against a pinned specification.

Reconciliation #46 asks whether observed reality matches what was desired. This asks what
was desired in the first place, and the two have different lifecycles: a configuration is
authored, layered and resolved long before anything observes it, and it stays valid when
nothing is observing at all.

Configuration is not arbitrary JSON. Every value is an assignment to a parameter declared
by a SpecificationPin, so an unknown key cannot be set and a typed key cannot be set twice.
Secrets are never values here: a secret-typed parameter carries a reference to a binding
resolved elsewhere, and this package stores no secret material at all.

fields.name: secret
fields.doc: A secret-typed parameter may only ever be assigned a reference, never a literal.

resources.name: ResolvedConfiguration
resources.doc:
A resolution, identified by a digest the caller computes over the resolved values. Stable
identity is what lets a reconciler say "still the same desired state" without re-reading
every value, and what lets a later reader tell two resolutions apart.

resources.name: ResolvedValue
resources.doc:
One resolved value, carrying the configuration it actually came from. That provenance is
the difference between a resolved bag of values and an explainable one: without it, nobody
can say which layer set a surprising value.

resources.name: SecretBinding
resources.doc:
Where a secret lives, never what it is. The reference is an opaque locator resolved by
whatever holds secrets; nothing in this package can dereference it.

resources.name: DeploymentConfiguration
resources.doc:
A deployment: the configuration a release is deployed with. Distinct from the release
itself, which is why it points at a resolution rather than at a Configuration — a deployment
is pinned to exactly the values that were resolved, not to whatever they resolve to later.

resources.name: DriftObservation
resources.doc:
F94-08: a reconciler consumes a resolution and owns none of it. It records what it observed
and whether that matched, and holds no parameter values of its own — so it cannot drift from
the desired state it is comparing against, because it does not keep a second copy.

resources.name: ProcessUnit
resources.doc:
An industrial device: setpoints and limits over a pinned process specification. The values
are operational rather than commercial, and nothing about the model changes for that.

resources.name: TenantPlan
resources.doc: A SaaS tenant: the option set sold to one customer.

resources.name: WorkspaceAgent
resources.doc:
F94-07, four shapes that look unrelated and parameterize identically.
A workspace agent: per-workspace options over a pinned agent specification.
